Durable design invariant, verified accurate: existing handlers (read/write/exit/brk/mprotect/munmap/gettimeofday/time/clock_gettime/rt_sigaction) really are arch-agnostic and just need a new register("<ARCH>", ...) row; mmap really does split into NativeMmapSyscall (modern 6-reg form, confirmed registered under AMD64/ARM64/MIPS64) vs NativeOldMmapSyscall/NativeMmap2Syscall (X86/ARM/MIPS32 legacy forms, confirmed distinct registrations in mod.rs); arch_prctl confirmed amd64-only. General enough to matter in any future new-arch-support session, not pinned to one file:line.

The "fd-table sync invariant" (Rust monotonic counter vs Python lowest-free, Rust owns fds it created, Python owns its own) is now documented verbatim as a named code comment section ("## Fd-table sync invariant (angr-8j16)") in both native/angr/src/procedures/read.rs and write.rs — criterion (b)-equivalent, dup of in-code docs. Also factually stale: the memory says fds with content_len==0 "fall back so Python's symbolic-file model owns the read," but read.rs now natively mints fresh symbolic bytes for open-but-empty fds (angr-gorvf.15) and serves bounded symbolic content via FileSystem::read_sym (angr-0xyq2 Phase 2), neither of which existed when this memory was written.

Content (two-level HashMap<&'static str, HashMap<u64,...>>, Borrow<str> resolving a runtime &str against &'static str keys, replacing a former linear iter().find() scan, angr-k95c) is now reproduced almost word-for-word as the doc comment directly on `struct NativeSyscallRegistry` in native/angr/src/syscalls/mod.rs (lines ~224-231). Criterion (b)-equivalent: duplicate of authoritative in-code documentation. Triage also flags closed_only.

Stale implementation reference: describes a "stub_syscall_1arg! macro in native/angr/src/syscalls/identity.rs" but the actual macro is the arbitrary-arity `stub_syscall!` defined in mod.rs (re-exported for use by identity.rs and others) — no `stub_syscall_1arg!` exists. The behavior it describes (ContinueSymbolic with fresh RustBV::symbolic sized to arch().bits(), naming mirrored from Python's syscall_stub) is already captured accurately in that macro's own doc comment in mod.rs. Criterion (e)/(f): stale file/macro-name reference, superseded by current in-code docs.

Durable architecture invariant: native syscall handlers (syscalls/) and native libc procedures (procedures/) are genuinely two separate dispatch tables keyed on different trigger conditions (raw syscall instruction vs libc call), confirmed by NativeReadSyscall/NativeWriteSyscall (syscalls/read.rs,write.rs) vs NativeRead/NativeWrite procedures (procedures/read.rs,write.rs) still existing as distinct impls. Worth a caveat: the "they share NO code currently, on purpose" sub-claim is now stale — syscalls/read.rs imports crate::procedures::strings::write_bv_bytes, so they do share a helper. The core lesson ("if you change one, also change the other") still holds and is the kind of cross-cutting gotcha worth keeping; bias to keep per instructions when torn.
